title: Rethinking LinterCop: Preparing for the Next Chapter
summary: LinterCop, a code analyzer for AL, faces architectural limitations that require fundamental redesign. The post explains tight coupling with the AL language, distribution challenges through GitHub, scope creep as a "Swiss Army Knife," and DevOps integration issues, leading to a proposed LinterCop 2.0 rebuild.
key_points: LinterCop generates 50 assets per release due to AL language version dependencies and breaking changes between versions
GitHub release distribution has rate limiting issues; moving to NuGet would require creating new package versions whenever AL Language updates
The analyzer scope has grown too broad, mixing language syntax rules with Business Central business logic recommendations, suggesting need for specialized analyzers
DevOps integration breaks in pre-release AL Language versions due to tight coupling, requiring fundamental architectural changes

quotes.text: Maintaining backward compatibility with third-party analyzers would slow down their own development. It's a trade-off that makes sense for me.
quotes.why_it_matters: Shows understanding of Microsoft's design decisions and the fundamental challenge for third-party tool developers
